# Chart

Bar, line and any other Chart.js chart, drawn from the theme: one component and one hook, data from the server.

> Requires the optional chart kit: `import { ChartHooks } from "shadcn_daisyui/charts"` and spread `ChartHooks` into the LiveSocket's hooks (dead views: `initCharts()`).

Needs the optional chart entry: import { ChartHooks } from "shadcn_daisyui/charts" and spread it into the LiveSocket's hooks (dead views: initCharts()). Chart.js ships inside the package (vendor/, pinned), so nothing loads from a CDN and the core shadcn_daisyui import stays free of it. Never put colours in the config: series take --chart-1…5 in order (or a dataset's color token), text --foreground / --muted-foreground, grid lines --border-color, and the tooltip is a popover. The chart redraws when the theme changes. Values in tooltips follow the value axis's ticks.format (Chart.js's Intl.NumberFormat options); the ticks show the same format, compacted ($25K). Labels arrive formatted - there is no date adapter. When LiveView changes config, the same chart moves to the new data.

## Usage guidance

Use when:

- Change over time: a line (one or a few series), or vertical bars for days and weeks
- A ranking or leaderboard: horizontal bars, longest first, each bar labelled at its end
- Progress through states: one horizontal stacked bar (resulted, needs a result, in progress, still to come)
- Comparing a handful of series: grouped or stacked bars with a legend

Don't use for:

- A single number, with or without a trend - use a number card
- Exact values people look up or copy - use a table (every chart also renders its numbers as a hidden table)
- More than five series - fold the rest into "Other", or split into small charts
- Comparing close values as slices - a pie or doughnut only shows part to whole at a glance

Sizing: The canvas is 16rem high (canvas_class="h-80" changes it); horizontal bar charts size themselves to their rows (36px each, 48px with the labels above the bars, plus 16px over the first row for its text). Bars are at most 24px thick with a 4px rounded end, lines 2px, text 12px.

Responsive: Charts fill their container's width and redraw on resize. On a narrow screen a leaderboard's end labels move above each bar with the name, so the bars keep their width (endLabels position: "above" keeps them there at every width), and a segment label shows only while its part is wide enough for it - the legend keeps every number. Put charts in a grid that stacks on phones (one column below sm).

iOS: Swift Charts: BarMark / LineMark / SectorMark with the same five chart colours, .chartXAxis(.hidden) for a leaderboard, and .accessibilityChartDescriptor for the numbers.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Figure | The <figure> with the hook; data-config holds the Chart.js config as JSON. |
| Canvas box | phx-update="ignore": Chart.js's container (role img, or application when clickable), focusable when it has tooltips. |
| Tooltip | A popover in the top layer: the label, then a colour key, the series name and the value per series. |
| Legend | Under the chart for two or more series; click a series to hide it. |
| Table | The numbers as a visually hidden table, captioned by label, for screen readers. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Height | 16rem; horizontal bars: 36px rows (48px with labels above) |
| Bars | max 24px thick, 4px rounded data end, square baseline |
| Stacked parts | 2px gap in the surface colour between parts |
| Segment labels | 12px, centred in the part; shown where the text's width + 8px fits inside the part and the bar is 16px thick or more; foreground or the surface colour, whichever reads 4.5:1 on the fill (black or white where neither does) |
| Lines | 2px, round joins; area fill at 10%; points hidden, 8px on hover with a 2px ring |
| Grid | 1px var(--border-color) on the value axis only, no axis lines |
| Text | 12px; ticks muted-foreground, legend and end labels foreground |
| Tooltip | popover surface, rounded-lg, shadow-lg, 12px; values tabular |

Tokens used: `chart-1`, `chart-2`, `chart-3`, `chart-4`, `chart-5`, `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `border-color`, `popover`

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Focuses the chart (when it has tooltips) |
| Arrow keys / Home / End | Move between labels (or a single bar's parts, or a doughnut's slices), showing the tooltip |
| Enter / Space | Sends on_click for the shown label or part |
| Escape | Hides the tooltip |

Role / ARIA: The canvas box is role="img" named by label (role="application" with aria-roledescription="chart" when on_click is set). A visually hidden <table> after it holds every number, with label as its caption: the canvas itself says nothing to a screen reader.

Focus: A 3px ring around the canvas box. Moving the pointer over the chart hands the tooltip back to the pointer.

Screen reader: The hidden table reads the numbers; while the arrow keys move, a polite live region reads the tooltip ("Mon 13: Sales $18,400").

Touch target: A tap anywhere in a bar's row (or a line's column) picks that label: the hit area is the row, not the painted bar.

Reduced motion: Animation is off under prefers-reduced-motion; otherwise new data moves in 300ms. Theme changes redraw instantly.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: partial - some web features are not yet native.

```swift
Chart(people) { person in
    BarMark(x: .value("Margin", person.margin), y: .value("Person", person.name))
        .foregroundStyle(Color.chart1)
    BarMark(x: .value("Rest", person.sale - person.margin), y: .value("Person", person.name))
        .foregroundStyle(Color.chart1.opacity(0.35))
        .annotation(position: .trailing) { Text(person.summary).font(.caption) }
}
.chartXAxis(.hidden)
.accessibilityChartDescriptor(LeaderboardDescriptor(people: people))
```

Swift Charts draws the same forms: stacked BarMarks for a leaderboard (an annotation at the end), LineMark + AreaMark for trends, SectorMark for part to whole. Use the five chart colours in order and give each chart an AXChartDescriptor so VoiceOver reads the numbers.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | string (required) | - |
| label | string (required): the accessible name and table caption | - |
| config | map (required): a Chart.js config - type, data, options | - |
| on_click | event: pushes %{id, key, series, index} for a clicked bar, point or slice | nil |
| target | phx-target for on_click (a LiveComponent) | nil |
| format | fn number -> text end, for the hidden table's numbers | digits grouped (24,500) |
| canvas_class | any (on the canvas box, e.g. h-80) | 16rem high |
| class | any (on the figure) | nil |
| dataset color | token: chart-1…5, muted, muted-foreground, primary, destructive, success, warning, info; "chart-1/40" = 40% opacity; a list colours each bar | chart-1…5 in order |
| dataset key | sent as series with a click | the label |
| data.keys | one key per label, sent as key with a click | the labels |
| options.plugins.endLabels.labels | one text per bar, drawn at its end | nil |
| options.plugins.endLabels.position | "auto" (at the bar's end; a horizontal bar's name and label move above it on a narrow screen) \| "above" (above the bar at every width) | "auto" |
| options.plugins.segmentLabels | true: on stacked bars, each part's value centred in it where the text and 4px either side fit (the bar 16px thick or more); a one-row stack's legend gives every part's number \| "legend": the legend's numbers only, nothing drawn on the bar | false |

## Bars by day

```heex
        options: %{scales: %{y: %{ticks: %{format: %{style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 0}}}}}
      }}
    />
  </.card_body>
</.card>
```

## Leaderboard

HEEx:

```heex
<%!-- Longest first; the margin is the darker part of each sale.
  Every bar is labelled at its end, so the value axis is hidden. --%>
<.chart
  id="leaderboard"
  label="Sales by person, this week"
  on_click="open_person"
  config={%{
    type: "bar",
    data: %{
      labels: Enum.map(@people, & &1.name),
      keys: Enum.map(@people, & &1.id),
      datasets: [
        %{label: "Margin", key: "margin", data: Enum.map(@people, & &1.margin), color: "chart-1"},
        %{label: "Rest of the sale", key: "rest", data: Enum.map(@people, &(&1.sale - &1.margin)), color: "chart-1/35"}
      ]
    },
    options: %{
      indexAxis: "y",
      scales: %{x: %{stacked: true, display: false, ticks: %{format: @usd}}, y: %{stacked: true}},
      plugins: %{endLabels: %{labels: Enum.map(@people, & &1.summary)}}
    }
  }}
/>

<%!-- def handle_event("open_person", %{"key" => id}, socket) -> open the sheet of that person's appointments --%>
```

---

# Code Block

Code, logs, payloads and diffs in a monospaced block with an optional header, line numbers and a copy button.

> Requires a JS hook: initialize with `initShadcnDaisyui()` (dead views) or the corresponding `Shadcn*` LiveView hook from `shadcn-daisyui.js`.

Rendered on the server with no syntax highlighting: the text is escaped and shown in the theme's monospace font. For colour, highlight on the server and pass one Phoenix.HTML.raw/1 fragment per line (e.g. Makeup.highlight_inner_html/1 on each line) with your own token CSS. Build lines in Elixir: a literal { inside a HEEx attribute opens an expression. Copy copies every line's plain text (no numbers, no markers) or copy_text, then shows a check for 2s, announces "Copied" and dispatches code-block:copied. Line numbers and diff markers are CSS generated content, so selecting the code never picks them up. Extra header buttons use class="code-block-action" (aria-pressed for a toggle such as wrap).

## Usage guidance

Use when:

- Text people read or copy exactly: a webhook or API payload, an integration log, an import error report
- A before/after change in a record's history - lines with :removed / :added
- Code in an AI chat reply - size="sm" inside the message

Don't use for:

- A short value inside a sentence - use inline code: <code class="rounded bg-muted px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-sm">
- Data people scan, sort or compare - use a table or a list
- Text people edit - use a textarea

Sizing: Default: text-sm monospace (line-height 1.625) with 16px padding in a 1px rounded-lg border. size="sm": text-xs with 12px padding, for output inside a card, a sheet or a chat reply. Cap long output with content_class (e.g. max-h-72) so it scrolls inside the block.

Responsive: Long lines scroll sideways inside the block, never the page, and the edges fade while there is more to see; wrap logs and prose-like output instead. The header title truncates. Without a header the copy button floats at the top end, always visible on touch screens.

iOS: Monospaced Text in a ScrollView with .textSelection(.enabled), and a copy button that writes UIPasteboard and announces "Copied".

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Block | The bordered surface; data-variant and data-size set its tone and scale. |
| Header (optional) | The title (filename or label, optional icon, truncates) and the actions. |
| Actions | Copy plus any :actions buttons; without a header they float at the top end. |
| Content | The <pre> scroll region: one span per line, a gutter of numbers, + / − markers. |
| Footer (optional) | A row under the code: Show more, Download. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Block | 1px var(--input) border, var(--radius-lg); transparent (dark: input at 30%); destructive: destructive/30 border, destructive text |
| Text | 0.875rem monospace, line-height 1.625 (sm: 0.75rem) |
| Padding | 1rem; 0.5rem between header and code, code and footer (sm: 0.75rem, 0.375rem under the header) |
| Header | title 0.875rem / 500 (sm 0.75rem), 1rem icon with a 6px gap (sm 0.875rem), 8px gap to the actions |
| Copy button | 1.5rem ghost icon button, 0.875rem icon, 44px hit area on touch |
| Floating actions | 0.75rem from the top and end (sm 0.5rem), on var(--background) with a 1px foreground/10 ring |
| Gutter | right-aligned numbers, min 1.5rem, 0.75rem from the text, muted-foreground |
| Diff lines | added: var(--muted) + "+"; removed: destructive/10 + "−" in destructive; highlighted: var(--muted) |
| Edge fade | min(12%, 2.5rem), over the first and last 6rem of scroll, only while there is more |
| Focus | 3px ring around the block, var(--ring) border |

Tokens used: `input`, `foreground`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `destructive`, `background`, `ring`

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves to the copy button (and any actions), then the code |
| Arrow keys / Page Up / Page Down | Scroll the focused code |
| Enter / Space | Copy, on the copy button |

Role / ARIA: The code is a <pre role="region" tabindex="0" dir="ltr"> named by the title (aria-labelledby) or label (default "Code"). Copy is a <button> labelled "Copy" (then "Copied"); its icons are aria-hidden; a polite live region announces "Copied".

Focus: The focused code region rings the whole block (3px ring, ring-coloured border). Floating actions appear while focus is inside the block.

Screen reader: Line numbers are silent (CSS alt text ""); diff markers read "Added" / "Removed" (set --code-block-added-label / --code-block-removed-label to translate). Highlighted lines are visual only: say why in the text around the block ("Row 42 has no email domain").

Touch target: The 24px copy button has a 44px hit area on touch screens, where floating actions stay visible.

Reduced motion: The floating actions' 150ms fade is dropped; the edge fade follows the scroll position, not time.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: partial - some web features are not yet native.

```swift
struct CodeBlock: View {
    let title: String?
    let code: String
    @State private var copied = false

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
            HStack {
                if let title {
                    Label(title, systemImage: "doc.text")
                        .font(.subheadline.weight(.medium))
                        .lineLimit(1)
                }
                Spacer()
                Button {
                    UIPasteboard.general.string = code
                    copied = true
                    AccessibilityNotification.Announcement("Copied").post()
                    Task { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2)); copied = false }
                } label: {
                    Image(systemName: copied ? "checkmark" : "doc.on.doc")
                }
                .buttonStyle(.borderless)
                .accessibilityLabel(copied ? "Copied" : "Copy")
            }
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                Text(code)
                    .font(.system(.footnote, design: .monospaced))
                    .textSelection(.enabled)
                    .fixedSize(horizontal: true, vertical: false)
            }
        }
        .padding()
        .overlay(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 10).strokeBorder(.separator))
    }
}
```

Monospaced Text in a ScrollView (horizontal; [.horizontal, .vertical] with a maxHeight for a long log), .textSelection(.enabled) so people can select part of it, and a copy button that writes UIPasteboard and announces "Copied". For a diff, one HStack per line in a LazyVStack: a +/− Text with .accessibilityLabel("Added" / "Removed") and a tinted .background. ShareLink suits a long log better than copy.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | string (required) | - |
| code | string (split into lines, HTML-escaped) | nil |
| lines | [string \| {variant, text} \| Phoenix.HTML.raw/1] - variant: added \| removed \| highlighted | [] |
| title | string (filename or label) | nil |
| icon | string (heroicon class) | nil |
| label | string (names the scroll region) | title, or "Code" |
| variant | default \| destructive | default |
| size | default \| sm | default |
| line_numbers | boolean | false |
| start_line | integer | 1 |
| highlight | [integer \| Range] (line numbers) | [] |
| wrap | boolean | false |
| copy | boolean | true |
| copy_text | string (what Copy copies) | the lines' text |
| copy_label / copied_label | string | "Copy" / "Copied" |
| content_class | any (on the scroll region, e.g. max-h-72) | nil |
| class | any | nil |
| :actions | slot (buttons before Copy, class code-block-action) | - |
| :footer | slot (a row under the code) | - |

# Collapsible

A single expandable/collapsible section.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Section | A `.collapse` block (collapse-arrow) holding a checkbox toggle. |
| Trigger | The `.collapse-title` row that expands/collapses the section. |
| Content | The `.collapse-content` region revealed when open. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger padding | 1rem block, padding-inline-end 2.5rem for the arrow |
| Trigger text | text-sm (0.875rem) font-medium |
| Content text | text-sm var(--muted-foreground) |
| Divider | border-bottom 1px var(--border-color) between sections |

Tokens used: `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `border-color`, `color-base-300`

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Move focus to the toggle |
| Space / Enter | Expand or collapse the section |

Role / ARIA: A disclosure: a toggle (checkbox) controls the visibility of an associated content region.

Focus: The toggle shows the ring-shadow focus outline.

Screen reader: Expose expanded/collapsed state (e.g. aria-expanded) so the open/closed status is announced.

Touch target: The full trigger row is tappable; ensure it reaches 2.75rem height on touch.

Reduced motion: Honor prefers-reduced-motion for the open/close height animation.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: native parity with the web component.

```swift
DisclosureGroup("@shadcn starred 3 repositories") {
  Text("@radix-ui/primitives")
  Text("@radix-ui/colors")
}
```

Maps directly to DisclosureGroup, which manages its own expanded state and chevron.

## Default

```html
<div class="card w-full">
  <div class="card-body py-1">
    <div class="collapse collapse-arrow">
      <input type="checkbox" />
      <div class="collapse-title font-medium">@shadcn starred 3 repositories</div>
      <div class="collapse-content space-y-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        <div class="rounded-md border border-base-300 px-3 py-2">@radix-ui/primitives</div>
        <div class="rounded-md border border-base-300 px-3 py-2">@radix-ui/colors</div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

# Data Table

A list page's table: the body scrolls under a header that stays put, columns sort, rows open the record, and ticked rows get a bulk bar.

> Requires a JS hook: initialize with `initShadcnDaisyui()` (dead views) or the corresponding `Shadcn*` LiveView hook from `shadcn-daisyui.js`.

Server-driven: each action sends an event and the LiveView answers with new assigns; the ShadcnDataTable hook only keeps checkboxes, scroll position and loading in step. On this static page only the client-side parts run (the sticky header, row focus and keys, ticking a checkbox); the full list page runs on the dev server (`/lab/data-table`).

Events (each payload also carries "table" => the component's id): dt:sort %{"key"} from a sortable header; dt:open %{"id"} from a row (click or Enter); dt:select %{"id", "shift"} from a row's checkbox; dt:select_all from the header checkbox; dt:select_matching from "Select all M rows"; dt:clear from Clear; dt:more when the end comes within ~200px (with more, once until the reply).

State: keep sort, search and filters in a ShadcnDaisyui.DataTable.State - State.from_params/2 in handle_params, State.toggle_sort/2 on dt:sort, State.select/4, select_all/2, keep_visible/2 and clear/1 for the ticks, State.run/3 to search, filter and sort in memory, State.to_params/2 for push_patch. Ticks live on the page, never in the URL.

Scrolling: a new sort, search or filter starts the body at the top; scroll_key keeps the body's scroll position in sessionStorage, so coming back to the list lands where the person left off; active_id highlights the row last opened and scrolls it into view. edge: on phones the table runs edge to edge (no side borders or rounding).

Alignment: the rightmost column shown at each width is right-aligned, header and cells, unless align="left"; the first column never is.

Layout: put the toolbar and table in an <.app_shell fill> page (or any flex column that fills the window) so the table takes the space left and only its body scrolls. These previews use a fixed-height flex column instead.

## Usage guidance

Use when:

- A list page where the table is the page: orders, customers, invoices
- Rows that open a record, with sorting, search and filters kept in the URL
- Bulk actions on ticked rows (mark paid, export, assign)

Don't use for:

- A handful of static rows - use <.table>, or <.table scroll> for a long one
- A record's own rows (activity, line items) - use <.table_card>
- Rows people edit in place - open the record instead

Sizing: A card that fills the space left: a 40px sticky header, text-sm rows with 10px vertical padding, a 44px checkbox column. table-fixed: give columns a width class (w-24, w-32) and let one column take the rest; cells truncate with …. The bulk bar is the header's height and covers the column labels, so rows never move.

Responsive: Hide columns with hide_below (sm 40rem, md 48rem, lg 64rem, xl 80rem); the rightmost column shown is right-aligned at every width. Ticking is a desktop job: the checkbox column and bulk bar show from md. edge puts the table edge to edge on phones. Never scroll sideways.

iOS: Table with selection and sortOrder on iPad / Mac; on iPhone a List of rows with NavigationLink, EditButton for selection and .searchable above it.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Card | .card.data-table: a flex column that takes the space left in its parent (flex-1, min-h-0). |
| Body | .data-table-scroll: the one scroll region, vertical only. |
| Header | Sticky th cells on the card fill with an inset 1px line. A sortable column is a button with an arrow (shown on hover/focus, solid when sorted) and aria-sort. |
| Checkbox column | With selectable, from md: the header box ticks every loaded row. |
| Row | Focusable, opens the record. Hover tint, ticked rows bg-muted, the row last opened bg-accent with a 2px primary mark at its start. |
| Bulk bar | While rows are ticked it covers the column labels: N selected, Select all M rows, :bulk, Clear. |
| Empty | No rows: <.empty variant="plain"> under the header, not as a row. |
| Loading | With more: a spinner row and the sentinel above it. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Header height | 2.5rem / 40px, sticky, z-10 |
| Cells | text-sm, 1rem inline / 0.625rem block padding, truncate |
| Checkbox column | 2.75rem / 44px (from 48rem) |
| Bulk bar | the header's height, from the checkbox column to the end |
| Sort arrow | 0.875rem, outside the label (before it on end-aligned columns) |
| Active row mark | 2px var(--primary) inset at the row's start |
| Load-more sentinel | 12.5rem / 200px above the spinner |

Tokens used: `card`, `card-foreground`, `border-color`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `accent`, `primary`, `foreground`, `ring`

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Reach the header buttons, then each row |
| Up / Down | Move to the previous / next row (keeps it under the header) |
| Enter | Open the focused row (dt:open) |
| Cmd/Ctrl + Enter | Open row_href in a new tab |
| Space | Tick the focused row (from md); Shift+Space ticks a range |
| Enter / Space on a header | Sort by that column (dt:sort) |

Role / ARIA: A real <table> (thead / tbody / th scope=col). Sortable headers hold a button and carry aria-sort (ascending, descending, none). Row checkboxes are labelled "Select" plus the row's first cell; the header box is "Select all orders". The bulk count is aria-live=polite.

Focus: Rows take focus (tabindex=0) with a 2px ring inside the row; a click on a link, button, input or label inside a row (or anything with data-row-ignore) doesn't open it, nor does a click that ends with text selected.

Screen reader: aria-sort announces the sorted column and direction; the bulk bar announces "N selected" as it changes; the loading row reads "Loading more orders".

Touch target: Rows are full-width tap targets; on phones there is no checkbox column (ticking is a desktop job). Bulk buttons are size="sm" on a pointer-first surface.

Reduced motion: Only the 150ms row hover tint transitions; scrolling a row into view is instant.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: partial - some web features are not yet native.

```swift
@State private var sortOrder = [KeyPathComparator(\Order.placed, order: .reverse)]
@State private var selection = Set<Order.ID>()

Table(orders, selection: $selection, sortOrder: $sortOrder) {
    TableColumn("Order", value: \.number)
    TableColumn("Customer", value: \.customer)
    TableColumn("Total", value: \.total) { Text($0.total, format: .currency(code: "USD")) }
}
.onChange(of: sortOrder) { _, order in orders.sort(using: order) }
.contextMenu(forSelectionType: Order.ID.self) { ids in
    Button("Export \(ids.count)") { export(ids) }
} primaryAction: { ids in open(ids) }
```

Table covers sortable columns, selection and opening a row on iPad and Mac. On iPhone it shows only its first column, so use a List of rows (NavigationLink to the record, EditButton for selection) and load more from the last row's onAppear.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | string (required) | - |
| rows | list (required) | - |
| row_id | fn row -> id | row.id |
| row_href | fn row -> path | nil (Cmd/Ctrl-click, middle click) |
| state | ShadcnDaisyui.DataTable.State | nil (sort + ticked rows) |
| selectable | boolean | false |
| more | boolean | false (sends dt:more near the end) |
| matching / all_matching | integer / boolean | nil / false |
| noun | {singular, plural} | {"row", "rows"} |
| active_id | any | nil (the row last opened) |
| scroll_key | string | nil |
| edge | boolean | false |
| target | phx-target | nil |
| :col label sort class align hide_below | slot | - |
| :bulk | slot (size="sm" buttons) | - |
| :empty title icon / :empty_action | slots | "No rows" |

## Default

HEEx:

```heex
<%!-- state = State.from_params(params, @opts), here sorted by "placed" newest first --%>
<div class="flex h-80 flex-col">
  <.data_table
    id="orders"
    rows={@rows}
    row_href={&~p"/orders/#{&1.id}"}
    state={@state}
    selectable
    noun={{"order", "orders"}}
    scroll_key="orders"
  >
    <:col :let={o} label="Order" sort="number" class="w-24 font-medium">{o.number}</:col>
    <:col :let={o} label="Customer" sort="customer">{o.customer}</:col>
    <:col :let={o} label="Owner" hide_below="lg" class="w-36">{o.owner}</:col>
    <:col :let={o} label="Status" hide_below="sm" class="w-28">
      <.badge variant={status_variant(o.status)}>{status_label(o.status)}</.badge>
    </:col>
    <:col :let={o} label="Placed" sort="placed" hide_below="md" class="w-32">{o.placed}</:col>
    <:col :let={o} label="Total" sort="total" class="w-28 tabular-nums">{o.total}</:col>
    <:bulk>
      <.button size="sm" variant="outline" phx-click="mark_paid">Mark paid</.button>
      <.button size="sm" variant="ghost" phx-click="export">Export</.button>
    </:bulk>
  </.data_table>
</div>
```

## Rows ticked

HEEx:

```heex
<%!-- every loaded row ticked, 240 match: the bulk bar offers them all --%>
<.data_table
  id="orders"
  rows={@rows}
  state={@state}
  selectable
  matching={@matching}
  all_matching={@all_matching}
  noun={{"order", "orders"}}
>
  …
  <:bulk>
    <.button size="sm" variant="outline" phx-click="mark_paid">Mark paid</.button>
    <.button size="sm" variant="ghost" phx-click="export">Export</.button>
  </:bulk>
</.data_table>

def handle_event("dt:select_all", _params, socket) do
  ids = Enum.map(socket.assigns.rows, & &1.id)
  {:noreply, update(socket, :state, &State.select_all(&1, ids))}
end

def handle_event("dt:select_matching", _params, socket),
  do: {:noreply, assign(socket, all_matching: true)}
```

# Empty

An empty state: an icon in a muted circle, a short title, one line saying what belongs here, and an optional action.

On its own it is a bordered card (variant="card"). Inside a table or card use variant="plain": a centred block with no border of its own. <.data_table>'s :empty slot renders it that way, below the header and not as a row. Say what belongs here and how to add it; a filter that matched nothing offers to clear the filters. Links inside the description are underlined.

## Usage guidance

Use when:

- A page or list with nothing in it yet ("No invoices yet")
- A search or filter that matched nothing - say so and offer to clear it
- An empty table or card - variant="plain" inside it

Don't use for:

- Errors - use an alert that says what went wrong and how to fix it
- Loading - use skeletons or a spinner, never an empty state that flips to content
- A field with no value - show "Not set" in muted text

Sizing: A 40px muted circle with a 20px icon, an 8px gap, a text-sm medium title, one text-sm muted line (max 24rem), and size="sm" actions 8px below. Card: 48px / 24px padding, rounded-xl, 1px border. Plain: 40px vertical padding, no border.

Responsive: Centred and balanced at every width; the text wraps within 24rem. Keep it to one action on phones.

iOS: ContentUnavailableView with a label, a description and actions - the same three parts.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Media | A 40px muted circle holding the icon or :media. |
| Title | Short, text-sm medium: "No invoices yet". |
| Description | One muted line: what belongs here, how it gets here. |
| Actions | Optional size="sm" buttons, centred. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Media | 2.5rem / 40px circle, var(--muted), 1.25rem icon |
| Gap | 0.5rem between parts; actions 0.5rem further |
| Card padding | 3rem block, 1.5rem inline; 1px border, var(--radius-xl) |
| Plain padding | 2.5rem block, no border |
| Description | text-sm, var(--muted-foreground), max 24rem |

Tokens used: `card`, `card-foreground`, `border-color`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

Role / ARIA: Plain text in a div; the circle is aria-hidden, so the title and description carry the meaning.

Focus: Not focusable itself; its action buttons keep their own focus rings.

Screen reader: Read as text. When it replaces results after a search or filter, the change should be announced (a live region on the result count, or move focus to it).

Touch target: Actions reach 44px on touch through the button sizes.

Reduced motion: No motion.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: native parity with the web component.

```swift
ContentUnavailableView {
    Label("No invoices yet", systemImage: "doc.text")
} description: {
    Text("Invoices you send show up here.")
} actions: {
    Button("New invoice") { newInvoice() }
}
```

ContentUnavailableView is the native empty state (and .search for a search that matched nothing); use it as a List's overlay when the list is empty.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| icon | string (heroicon class) | nil |
| title | string | nil |
| variant | card \| plain | card |
| class | any | nil |
| inner_block | slot (one muted line) | - |
| :media | slot (replaces the icon in the circle) | - |
| :actions | slot (size="sm" buttons) | - |

## Card

HEEx:

```heex
<.empty icon="hero-document-text" title="No invoices yet">
  Invoices you send show up here.
  <:actions><.button size="sm" navigate={~p"/invoices/new"}>New invoice</.button></:actions>
</.empty>
```

# Item

A versatile row for displaying content with media, title, description, and actions.

## Usage guidance

Use when:

- Settings rows, notification rows, and file/member lists: one object per row with an action
- A list where each row needs more than a label (media, two lines of text, buttons)

Don't use for:

- Form fields - use <.field> / <.input>, which own labels and errors
- Dense tabular data you compare across rows - use <.table>
- Menu commands - use a dropdown menu or command palette

Sizing: Default 14px/16px padding; sm 10px/12px for denser lists; xs 8px/10px inside menus and popovers. Titles clamp to one line, descriptions to two.

Responsive: Rows wrap: header/footer always span the full width, and actions drop under the text when space runs out. On compact screens keep one primary action per row.

iOS: A List row: HStack of image, VStack(title, subtitle), Spacer, trailing control. Use .listRowInsets to match the size scale.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Item | data-slot=item row (a <div>, or an <a> when linked). |
| Media (optional) | Leading icon, avatar, or 40px image; top-aligns when there's a description. |
| Content | Title (1 line) and description (2 lines, muted). |
| Actions (optional) | Trailing buttons, badges, or a chevron. |
| Header / footer (optional) | Full-width rows above / below. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Padding (default / sm / xs) | 14px 16px / 10px 12px / 8px 10px |
| Gap (default / sm / xs) | 14px / 10px / 8px |
| Radius | var(--radius-md), 1px border (transparent unless outline) |
| Title | 14px / 500, line-clamp 1 |
| Description | 14px muted-foreground, line-clamp 2 (12px at xs) |
| Image media | 40px (sm 32px, xs 24px), var(--radius-sm) |
| Muted variant | muted at 50% |
| Link hover | muted background, 100ms |

Tokens used: `border-color`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `ring`, `primary`

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Focus a linked item, or the buttons in its actions |
| Enter | Follow a linked item |

Role / ARIA: A plain container; <.item_group> is role=list, so give each item role=listitem. Linked items render a real <a>.

Focus: Linked items show the 3px ring (border-color ring + ring shadow). Don't nest interactive controls inside a linked item - keep actions outside or use a non-link item.

Screen reader: Title then description read in order. Icon media is decorative (aria-hidden); give icon-only action buttons an aria-label.

Touch target: Default rows are 48px+ tall; icon-only actions need a 44pt hit area on touch (btn-sm square is 32px - pad the row or use btn on touch).

Reduced motion: Only a 100ms color change on hover; nothing moves.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: partial - some web features are not yet native.

```swift
HStack(spacing: 14) {
    Image(systemName: "shield.lefthalf.filled")
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
        Text("Security Alert").font(.subheadline.weight(.medium))
        Text("New login detected from unknown device.")
            .font(.subheadline).foregroundStyle(.secondary).lineLimit(2)
    }
    Spacer()
    Button("Review") {}.buttonStyle(.bordered).controlSize(.small)
}
.padding(.vertical, 14).padding(.horizontal, 16)
.overlay(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8).stroke(Color.sdBorder))
```

Inside a List, the row is the item (drop the overlay). The outline variant maps to a stroked RoundedRectangle; muted to a .fill(Color.sdMuted.opacity(0.5)) background.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| variant | default \| outline \| muted | default |
| size | default \| sm \| xs | default |
| href / navigate / patch | string | nil (renders a link) |
| :media variant | default \| icon \| image | default |
| slots | :media :title :description :actions :header :footer | - |

## Variants

HEEx:

```heex
<.item>
  <:title>Default Variant</:title>
  <:description>Standard styling with subtle background and borders.</:description>
  <:actions><.button variant="outline" size="sm">Open</.button></:actions>
</.item>
<.item variant="outline">…</.item>
<.item variant="muted">…</.item>
```

```html
<div class="flex w-full max-w-md flex-col gap-6">
  <div data-slot="item" data-variant="default" data-size="default">
    <div data-slot="item-content">
      <div data-slot="item-title">Default Variant</div>
      <p data-slot="item-description">Standard styling with subtle background and borders.</p>
    </div>
    <div data-slot="item-actions"><button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm">Open</button></div>
  </div>
  <div data-slot="item" data-variant="outline" data-size="default">
    <div data-slot="item-content">
      <div data-slot="item-title">Outline Variant</div>
      <p data-slot="item-description">Outlined style with clear borders and transparent background.</p>
    </div>
    <div data-slot="item-actions"><button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm">Open</button></div>
  </div>
  <div data-slot="item" data-variant="muted" data-size="default">
    <div data-slot="item-content">
      <div data-slot="item-title">Muted Variant</div>
      <p data-slot="item-description">Subdued appearance with muted colors for secondary content.</p>
    </div>
    <div data-slot="item-actions"><button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm">Open</button></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

HEEx:

```heex
<.item_group class="max-w-sm">
  <%= for {person, i} <- Enum.with_index(@people) do %>
    <.item_separator :if={i > 0} />
    <.item role="listitem">
      <:media><.avatar fallback={person.initials} class="w-10" /></:media>
      <:title>{person.username}</:title>
      <:description>{person.email}</:description>
      <:actions>
        <.button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label={"Add #{person.username}"}><.icon name="hero-plus" /></.button>
      </:actions>
    </.item>
  <% end %>
</.item_group>
```

```html
<div role="list" data-slot="item-group" class="max-w-sm rounded-xl border border-base-300 bg-card p-2">
  <div role="listitem" data-slot="item" data-variant="default" data-size="default">
    <div data-slot="item-media" data-variant="default"><div class="avatar avatar-placeholder"><div class="w-10 rounded-full"><span class="text-sm font-medium">SC</span></div></div></div>
    <div data-slot="item-content"><div data-slot="item-title">shadcn</div><p data-slot="item-description">shadcn@vercel.com</p></div>

  </div>

  <div role="listitem" data-slot="item" data-variant="default" data-size="default">
    <div data-slot="item-media" data-variant="default"><div class="avatar avatar-placeholder"><div class="w-10 rounded-full"><span class="text-sm font-medium">ML</span></div></div></div>
```

# Kbd

Displays keyboard keys or shortcuts inline.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Key | Inline kbd element styled as a keycap. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Radius | var(--radius-sm) |
| Border | 1px var(--border-color) |
| Background | var(--muted) |
| Text | var(--muted-foreground), 0.75rem |

Tokens used: `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `border-color`

## Accessibility

Role / ARIA: Native kbd element marking keyboard input. Semantic but non-interactive; it labels a shortcut, it does not trigger one.

Focus: Not focusable.

Screen reader: Read inline as its text content. Spell out non-obvious symbols (write Command K rather than relying on the glyph alone) where clarity matters.

Touch target: Decorative; no hit area.

Reduced motion: No motion.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: guidance only - no native component yet.

```swift
Text("⌘K")
    .font(.caption.monospaced())
    .padding(.horizontal, 4)
    .background(Color(.systemGray6), in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 4))
```

No native keycap view; SwiftUI's .keyboardShortcut(_:) wires the actual shortcut while a styled Text shows the hint.

## Default

```html
<p class="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
  Press <kbd class="kbd">⌘</kbd> <kbd class="kbd">K</kbd> to open the command menu.
</p>
```

---

# List

Vertical rows of items with avatars and actions.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| List | Rounded, bordered <ul class=list> container. |
| List row | list-row with avatar, primary/secondary text, and a trailing action. |
| Row divider | 1px border-color between rows. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Radius | rounded-xl container in the example |
| Border | 1px border-color outer, 1px divider between rows |
| Font | 0.875rem base; secondary text text-xs muted-foreground |
| Padding | p-3 per row, gap-3 between row elements |

Tokens used: `card`, `border-color`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

Role / ARIA: Semantic <ul>/<li>; the per-row action buttons carry their own aria-labels.

Focus: Only the in-row controls (e.g. the more-options button) are focusable.

Screen reader: Rows read as list items; trailing icon buttons announce via aria-label.

Touch target: Row action buttons should meet the 44pt touch target on touch surfaces.

Reduced motion: Static; no animation to suppress.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: native parity with the web component.

```swift
List(people) { person in
    HStack {
        avatar(person)
        VStack(alignment: .leading) {
            Text(person.name)
            Text(person.email).font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        Spacer()
        Menu { ... } label: { Image(systemName: "ellipsis") }
    }
}
```

Native List with custom rows is the direct equivalent.

## Default

```html
<ul class="list w-full max-w-md rounded-xl border border-base-300">
  <li class="list-row flex items-center gap-3 p-3">
    <div class="avatar avatar-placeholder">
      <div class="w-8 rounded-full"><span class="text-xs">AB</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="flex-1">
      <div class="font-medium">Alex Brown</div>
      <div class="text-xs text-muted-foreground">alex@example.com</div>
    </div>
    <button class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm btn-square" aria-label="More options"><span class="hero-ellipsis-horizontal size-4" aria-hidden="true"></span></button>
  </li>
  <li class="list-row flex items-center gap-3 p-3">
    <div class="avatar avatar-placeholder">
      <div class="w-8 rounded-full"><span class="text-xs">CD</span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="flex-1">
      <div class="font-medium">Casey Day</div>
      <div class="text-xs text-muted-foreground">casey@example.com</div>
    </div>
    <button class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm btn-square" aria-label="More options"><span class="hero-ellipsis-horizontal size-4" aria-hidden="true"></span></button>
  </li>
</ul>
```

# Number Card

A label, a big number, a line under it, and a faint trend behind the number: a dashboard's headline figures.

> Requires the optional chart kit: `import { ChartHooks } from "shadcn_daisyui/charts"` and spread `ChartHooks` into the LiveSocket's hooks (dead views: `initCharts()`).

The trend is a <.chart> line with its axes, grid, legend, tooltip and points hidden and its area filled, so it needs the chart entry (shadcn_daisyui/charts); without it the card still shows the number and the line under it. Labels name the rows of the trend's hidden table ({"Mon 13", 18_400}); bare numbers are numbered 1, 2, 3. A nil (a day with nothing to count) in the middle is bridged, never a gap; nils at either end are dropped, so the line runs edge to edge rather than stopping in a cliff; with fewer than two points left there is no trend. The value, the line under it and the changes arrive formatted from the server. A change is good news (green) when it moved the way `good` says, bad news (red) the other way, neutral when flat; its sign and arrow say the same, never colour alone. A linked card's label is the link, stretched over the card, so the help stays its own button.

## Usage guidance

Use when:

- A dashboard's headline figures: today's sales, appointments, close rate
- One number that matters, with how it got there as a faint trend
- A number with its breakdown under it ("Margin $14,700 (35%)") and its change on another period as badges (vs PP)
- A number people open to see what's behind it: the whole card is a link

Don't use for:

- Several series or values people compare - use a chart
- A list of figures with labels - use a table or a description list
- A status (on track, late) - say it in words with a badge, not a number

Sizing: Card padding 24px; the label 14px / 500 muted, with a 16px ? after it; the number 30px / 600, the line under it 14px muted, the change badges 12px, 8px below it. The trend fills the lower 60% of the card at 50% opacity behind the text and the badges, its peaks as clear as the rest of it.

Responsive: Lay a row of cards out in a grid: one column on phones, two from sm, four from lg. The number never wraps mid-figure; keep it short (format it on the server: $42K, 38%).

iOS: A GroupBox with the label, a .title.weight(.semibold) number and a caption, over a Chart with an AreaMark + LineMark and .chartXAxis(.hidden) / .chartYAxis(.hidden).

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Card | The card surface (rounded-xl, 1px border, shadow-sm). It doesn't clip, so the help can float over its edge; the trend clips itself. |
| Label | What the number is, sentence case, no colon; the link's text when the card is a link. |
| Help | A ? after the label; what the number counts, in a popover on hover, focus or tap. |
| Value | The number, formatted on the server, proportional figures. |
| Line under | A comparison or breakdown: "Margin $14,700 (35%)". |
| Changes | Per period, an outline badge naming it (vs PP), then the difference and the change, tinted good, bad or neutral, each edged in its own tone. |
| Trend | A filled line chart behind the text and badges, edge to edge inside the card's border, aria-hidden, with its own hidden table. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Padding | 1.5rem (24px) |
| Label | 0.875rem / 500, muted-foreground |
| Value | 1.875rem / 600, letter-spacing -0.025em |
| Line under | 0.875rem, muted-foreground |
| Help | 16px icon, 44px target on touch, 16rem popover |
| Changes | 12px badges, 8px apart (4px within a period), 8px below the line; tints of success and destructive on the card, a 1px border in the badge's tone at 30% over the card (the period's: foreground at 18%); text at least 4.5:1 |
| Trend | lower 60% of the card, edge to edge (no auto padding), the peak a sixth of its height below the top and the range at least a fifth of the top value (a flat series is a level line), 50% opacity, 2px line, 25% area fill, gaps bridged |

Tokens used: `card`, `border-color`, `foreground`, `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `chart-1`, `color-success`, `destructive`, `popover`

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | The card's link (when it is one), then the help |
| Enter | Opens the card's link |

Role / ARIA: Text (a <p> each for the label, the number and the line under it), the label a link when the card is one, the help a button described by its text (role=tooltip). The trend's canvas is aria-hidden; its numbers are in a visually hidden table named "<label> trend".

Focus: A linked card shows the 3px ring around the whole card; the help shows it around the ? and opens its text.

Screen reader: Reads the label ("Sales, link"), the number, the line under it and the changes ("vs PP, +$8,000, +24%"), then the trend's table. The help button reads "About Sales" and its text.

Touch target: A linked card is one big target; the help's ? has a 44px target and opens on tap.

Reduced motion: The trend doesn't animate under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: guidance only - no native component yet.

```swift
GroupBox {
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
        Text("Sales").font(.subheadline.weight(.medium)).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        Text("$42,000").font(.title.weight(.semibold))
        Text("Margin $14,700 (35%)").font(.subheadline).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
    }
    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
}
.background(alignment: .bottom) {
    Chart(trend) { AreaMark(x: .value("Day", $0.day), y: .value("Sales", $0.value)) }
        .chartXAxis(.hidden).chartYAxis(.hidden)
        .foregroundStyle(Color.chart1.opacity(0.25))
        .frame(height: 60)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
}
```

Keep the number in Text so VoiceOver reads it; the trend behind it is decoration (accessibilityHidden), with the comparison said in words under the number.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | string (required) | - |
| label | string (required) | - |
| value | string (required): the number, formatted | - |
| trend | [number] or [{label, number}], oldest first; nil at either end is dropped | [] (no trend) |
| color | the trend's colour token | chart-1 |
| help | string: what the number counts, in plain words (a ? beside the label) | nil |
| navigate / patch / href | the whole card is a link (the label is its text) | nil |
| format | fn number -> text end, for the trend's hidden table | digits grouped |
| class | any | nil |
| inner_block | slot: the line under the number | - |
| :change | slot, one per period: vs ("vs PP"), by ("+$8,000"), percent ("+24%"), direction (up/down/flat), good (up/down/none, default up) | - |

## A row of number cards

HEEx:

```heex
<div class="grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4">
  <.number_card
    id="sales"
    label="Sales"
    value="$42,000"
    help="Every sale booked this week, at its sold price."
    trend={@sales_trend}
    patch={~p"/dashboard?open=sales"}
  >
    Margin $14,700 (35%)
    <:change vs="vs PP" by="+$8,000" percent="+24%" direction="up" />
  </.number_card>
  <.number_card id="appointments" label="Appointments" value="30" trend={@appointments_trend}>
    vs. 27 last Tuesday
  </.number_card>
  <.number_card
    id="close-rate"
    label="Close rate"
    value="38%"
    help="Visits that sold, out of visits that happened."
    trend={@close_rate_trend}
    color="chart-3"
  >
    11 of 29 run
    <:change vs="vs PP" by="-2.4 pts" percent="-6%" direction="down" />
  </.number_card>
  <.number_card id="average-sale" label="Average sale" value="$3,818">
    2 cancellations
  </.number_card>
</div>
```

# Stat

Compact blocks for key metrics.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Stats container | Card surface holding one or more stat cells side by side. |
| Title | Metric label, 0.875rem, muted-foreground. |
| Value | The large headline figure, font-weight 600. |
| Description | Trend/context line in muted-foreground. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Radius | var(--radius-xl) on the stats card |
| Border | 1px border-color around the card; 1px divider between cells |
| Shadow | var(--shadow-sm) |
| Title / desc font | 0.875rem, muted-foreground |
| Value weight | 600 |

Tokens used: `card`, `card-foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `border-color`

## Accessibility

Role / ARIA: Presentational layout - a styled set of divs; the value reads as plain text.

Focus: Not focusable; no interactive elements within a stat cell.

Screen reader: Title, value, and description read in document order as adjacent text.

Touch target: Not interactive; no hit-target requirement.

Reduced motion: Static; no animation to suppress.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: partial - some web features are not yet native.

```swift
GroupBox {
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
        Text("Total Revenue").font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        Text("$45,231").font(.title2.weight(.semibold))
        Text("+20.1% from last month").font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
    }
}
```

Compose a labeled VStack (or GroupBox per metric); lay multiple out in a Grid/HStack.

## Default

```html
<div class="stats w-full">
  <div class="stat">
    <div class="stat-title">Total Revenue</div>
    <div class="stat-value">$45,231</div>
    <div class="stat-desc">+20.1% from last month</div>
  </div>
  <div class="stat">
    <div class="stat-title">Subscriptions</div>
    <div class="stat-value">+2,350</div>
    <div class="stat-desc">+180.1% from last month</div>
  </div>
  <div class="stat">
    <div class="stat-title">Active Now</div>
    <div class="stat-value">+573</div>
    <div class="stat-desc">+201 since last hour</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

---

# Table

A responsive table for displaying rows of data.

## Usage guidance

Use when:

- Scanning and comparing records across a few columns
- Static or lightly interactive row data (use <.table> with <:col> slots)
- A long list in a card that fills the window: <.table scroll> keeps the header put while the body scrolls

Don't use for:

- A list page with sorting, selection or filters - use data-table
- Compact screens with many columns - restructure as a card list

Sizing: text-sm rows; wrap in a card for the border (class recipe) - no extra cell padding.

Responsive: Tables don't shrink gracefully: below medium, show fewer columns or switch to stacked cards/list rows.

iOS: A List with custom row layout; columns become labeled lines within the row.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Table | Native table element at text-sm. |
| Header | th cells in muted-foreground with medium weight. |
| Row | tbody rows with hairline borders; hover tints with muted. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Font | 0.875rem (text-sm) |
| Header color | var(--muted-foreground), weight 500 |
| Cell border | var(--border-color) |
| Row hover | var(--muted) background |

Tokens used: `muted-foreground`, `border-color`, `muted`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Move through any interactive cell content (links, buttons) |

Role / ARIA: Native table / thead / tbody / th / td with their implicit table roles. Header cells should scope columns; the demo uses semantic th elements.

Focus: The table itself is not focusable; interactive cell content keeps its own focus order and rings.

Screen reader: Table semantics let users navigate by row and column. Provide a caption or surrounding heading for context.

Touch target: Interactive cell content (action buttons/links) should meet the 44pt minimum on touch.

Reduced motion: Row hover is a short color transition only; nothing moves.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: partial - some web features are not yet native.

```swift
Table(people) {
    TableColumn("Name", value: \.name)
    TableColumn("Email", value: \.email)
}
```

Table is full-featured on macOS/iPadOS; on iPhone a List of rows is the practical equivalent, so behavior differs by size class.

## Default

HEEx:

```heex
<.table id="invoices" rows={@invoices}>
  <:col :let={invoice} label="Invoice">{invoice.id}</:col>
  <:col :let={invoice} label="Status">{invoice.status}</:col>
  <:col :let={invoice} label="Method">{invoice.method}</:col>
  <:col :let={invoice} label="Amount">{invoice.amount}</:col>
</.table>
```

```html

    <thead>

        <th>Invoice</th>
        <th>Status</th>
        <th>Method</th>
        <th class="text-right">Amount</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td class="font-medium">INV001</td>
        <td><span class="badge badge-secondary">Paid</span></td>
        <td>Credit Card</td>
        <td class="text-right">$250.00</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td class="font-medium">INV002</td>

        <td>PayPal</td>
        <td class="text-right">$150.00</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td class="font-medium">INV003</td>
        <td><span class="badge badge-error">Unpaid</span></td>
        <td>Bank Transfer</td>
        <td class="text-right">$350.00</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>

```

# Table Card

A card of rows with a title and description: a record's activity, its line items, its contacts.

The rightmost column is right-aligned unless align="left" (on phones only with grid, since stacked cells read top to bottom). :empty renders as the only row when rows is empty ("Nothing has happened yet."). row_class styles a row (a muted cancelled line). Row actions are a ⋯ <.dropdown_menu align="end"> in the last column: the card doesn't clip, so the menu opens in full over its edge, on the last row too (the rows at the corners round with the card instead). Rows are one height - a row of text's - whether or not they hold a ⋯ menu, a small button or a badge (those sit in the row's padding), and the :empty row matches them, so cards side by side line up; taller content (two lines) still makes its row taller. The record page on the dev server (`/lab/data-table/:id`) uses it for Items and Activity.

## Usage guidance

Use when:

- Rows that belong to one record: activity, line items, contacts, payments
- A few columns that read as a list on phones (stacked) or stay side by side (grid)

Don't use for:

- A list page with sorting, selection and filters - use <.data_table>
- Rows people compare across many columns - use <.table>
- One object per row with media and actions - use <.item>

Sizing: Card header 24px padding (16px under it): card-title, a muted description, :actions on the right. Rows text-sm, 12px / 24px padding, 16px column gap, 1px lines edge to edge; the last row's padding is the space under it. Column labels are a muted 500 row.

Responsive: From sm the columns share the width equally (2-6 columns) under a label row. On phones each row stacks its cells, unless grid (a grid-cols class) keeps them side by side at every width - use it for short numeric columns such as Qty and Price.

iOS: A Section in an inset-grouped List (header and footer text), one row per item.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Header | card-title, muted description, :actions on the right. |
| Label row | Column labels, muted 500, from sm (role=columnheader). |
| Row | A grid row of cells, 1px line under it, edge to edge. |
| Empty row | :empty, centred muted text, when there are no rows. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Header padding | 1.5rem 1.5rem 1rem |
| Row padding | 0.75rem block, 1.5rem inline |
| Column gap | 1rem (0.25rem between stacked cells) |
| Label row | 0.5rem block padding, var(--muted-foreground), 500 |
| Columns | equal shares for 2-6 columns from 40rem, or the grid class |

Tokens used: `card`, `card-foreground`, `border-color`, `muted-foreground`, `foreground`

## Accessibility

Role / ARIA: A section holding role=table (named by the title) with rowgroups, rows, columnheaders and cells, so the stacked phone layout keeps table semantics.

Focus: Nothing focusable of its own; links and buttons in cells or :actions keep their rings.

Screen reader: Read as a table with column headers; stacked cells on phones still announce their column.

Touch target: Interactive content in cells (links, buttons) should reach 44px on touch.

Reduced motion: No motion.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: partial - some web features are not yet native.

```swift
Section {
    ForEach(events) { event in
        LabeledContent {
            Text(event.at, format: .dateTime.month().day())
        } label: {
            Text(event.what)
            Text(event.by).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
    }
} header: {
    Text("Activity")
} footer: {
    Text("Everything that happened to #1042.")
}
```

An inset-grouped List Section matches the card; LabeledContent puts the trailing value on the right like the rightmost column. Use Grid for true columns on iPad.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | string (required) | - |
| title / description | string | nil |
| rows | list (required) | - |
| row_id | fn row -> DOM id | nil |
| row_class | fn row -> classes | nil |
| grid | string (grid-cols class) | nil (stack on phones) |
| :col label class align | slot | - |
| :actions | slot (right of the title) | - |
| :empty | slot (the only row when there are none) | - |

## Activity

HEEx:

```heex
<.table_card
  id="activity"
  title="Activity"
  description="Everything that happened to #1042."
  rows={@events}
  row_id={&"event-#{&1.id}"}
>
  <:actions><.button size="sm" variant="outline" phx-click="add_note">Add note</.button></:actions>
  <:col :let={e} label="Event" class="font-medium">{e.what}</:col>
  <:col :let={e} label="By" class="text-muted-foreground">{e.by}</:col>
  <:col :let={e} label="When">{e.at}</:col>
  <:empty>Nothing has happened yet.</:empty>
</.table_card>
```

```html

          Status: Paid
        </div>

```

## Line items

HEEx:

```heex
<.table_card
  id="items"
  title="Items"
  description="What's on the order."
  rows={@items}
  grid="grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_2.5rem_6rem]"
>
  <:col :let={i} label="Item">{i.name}</:col>
  <:col :let={i} label="Qty" class="tabular-nums">{i.qty}</:col>
```

---

# Table Toolbar

The one row above a data table: saved views or the count, search, a Filters sheet, and the filters that are on as chips.

> Requires a JS hook: initialize with `initShadcnDaisyui()` (dead views) or the corresponding `Shadcn*` LiveView hook from `shadcn-daisyui.js`.

The toolbar is one form: it sends dt:filter (on change and submit) with q (the search, debounced 200ms), each :filter's value (a multiple select posts a list, cleared posts "") and sort. Removing a chip sends dt:unfilter %{"key"}; Clear all sends dt:reset. Every payload carries "table" => the toolbar's id.

Apply it with State.put_search/2, State.put_filters/4 and State.parse_sort/3 (value first: State.parse_sort(params["sort"], state, opts)), then push_patch to State.to_params/2. State.chips/3 turns the filters into chips ("Open or Paid"); a saved view's own filter is a {key, label, :fixed} chip that can't be removed.

The Filters sheet: each :filter under its label, applied as it changes (the sheet stays open); on phones a Sort by select (the first of sorts is the default order, posted as ""); a footer with Clear all and "Show N orders", which closes it. On this static page the sheet, pickers, views menu and chips run, but nothing is sent; the full list page runs on the dev server (`/lab/data-table`).

## Usage guidance

Use when:

- Above a <.data_table>: search, filters and saved views of one list
- Filters that belong in the URL, so a view can be bookmarked and Back restores it
- Saved views people switch between (All, Open, Mine), each a patch link with its count

Don't use for:

- A short list with nothing to filter - a heading and the table are enough
- Filters that change the whole page (date range for a dashboard) - put them in the page header
- Search that only the server can run across records - use <.command on_search>

Sizing: One row, 8px gaps: views (a tab nav) or a muted text-sm count, the h-9 search (16rem; 14rem beside views), an outline Filters button with a 20px primary count pill, then :more. Chips sit 8px under the row in a reveal.

Responsive: Phones: without views the search takes the row; beside views it shrinks to 7rem. Filters goes icon-only (the label stays for screen readers), :more hides, and the sheet adds a Sort by select (from sorts). The row never wraps: views fold into the Views menu, chips into +N.

iOS: .searchable for the search, .searchScopes or a segmented Picker for views, and a toolbar button that opens a filter sheet (a Form of pickers).

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Views | A <.tab_nav> of patch links with counts; an edited view shows a dot; overflow and the menu entries go in the Views menu. |
| Count | Without views: "N orders", or "N of M" while filtered. |
| Search | An input with a magnifier, name q, debounced 200ms. |
| Filters button | Outline button that opens the sheet, with the number of filters on. |
| More | Trailing controls (Export, Columns), hidden on phones. |
| Chips row | A <.chip_row> in a <.reveal>: removable chips, fixed chips, a stack for a filter with several values (named after its :filter), then :save and Clear all. |
| Filters sheet | A <.sheet>: one field per filter, Sort by on phones, Clear all + Show N. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Row | flex, 0.5rem gaps, never wraps |
| Search | 16rem (14rem beside views from 40rem, 7rem on phones) |
| Filters count | 1.25rem pill, var(--primary), text-xs |
| Edited dot | 0.375rem, var(--primary) |
| Chips row | 0.5rem under the row, 180ms reveal |
| Sheet fields | 1rem apart, label text-sm 500, 0.5rem above its picker |

Tokens used: `muted`, `muted-foreground`, `primary`, `primary-foreground`, `secondary`, `input`, `border-color`, `popover`, `ring`

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Views, search, Filters, :more, then the chips |
| Enter / Space | Open the Filters sheet |
| Esc | Close the sheet (or an open picker inside it first) |
| Enter in the search | Submit the form (dt:filter) at once |

Role / ARIA: The views are a nav named "Views" (aria-current on the active link). The search is type=search labelled by its placeholder. The Filters button has aria-haspopup=dialog and aria-controls the sheet; the count reads "2 on". Chips are a group named "Active filters"; each × is "Remove filter: Status: Open".

Focus: Opening the sheet moves focus into it; closing returns it to the Filters button. Removing a chip moves focus to its neighbour.

Screen reader: The count is plain text ("12 of 240"); the Filters button announces how many filters are on; the views menu names the active view.

Touch target: On phones Filters is a 44px icon button and the sheet's pickers use full_width (44px on touch).

Reduced motion: The chips row slides 180ms and chips fade; both drop to instant under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: partial - some web features are not yet native.

```swift
@State private var query = ""
@State private var view: OrderView = .all
@State private var showFilters = false

OrdersList(query: query, view: view, filters: filters)
    .searchable(text: $query, prompt: "Search orders")
    .searchScopes($view) {
        ForEach(OrderView.allCases) { Text($0.label).tag($0) }
    }
    .toolbar {
        Button("Filters", systemImage: "line.3.horizontal.decrease.circle") { showFilters = true }
    }
    .sheet(isPresented: $showFilters) { FiltersForm(filters: $filters) }
```

.searchable with .searchScopes covers search and views; filters go in a sheet holding a Form of Pickers (a multi-select is a List with selection). Show active filters as a horizontal row of removable capsules above the list if they matter at a glance.

## Props

| Name | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | string (required) | - |
| search / placeholder | string | "" / "Search…" |
| shown / total | integer | nil ("N orders", "N of M" when filtered) |
| noun | {singular, plural} | {"row", "rows"} |
| views | [%{key, label, count, path, active, edited}] | [] |
| menu | [%{key, label, group, icon, active, path \| click}] | [] |
| chips | [{key, label} \| {key, label, :fixed} \| {key, [{value, label}]} \| {key, [{value, label}], :fixed}] | [] |
| sort / sorts | "key:dir" / [{label, "key:dir"}] | "" / [] |
| target | phx-target | nil |
| :filter key label | slot (one select or combobox named key) | - |
| :more | slot (hidden on phones) | - |
| :save | slot (end of the chips row) | - |

## With views

HEEx:

```heex
<.table_toolbar
  id="orders-toolbar"
  search={@state.search}
  placeholder="Search orders"
  shown={@matching}
  total={@total}
  noun={{"order", "orders"}}
  views={
    for v <- @views do
      %{key: v.key, label: v.label, count: v.count, path: ~p"/orders?view=#{v.key}",
        active: v.key == @view.key, edited: v.key == @view.key and State.filtered?(@state, @opts)}
    end
  }
  menu={[%{key: "manage", label: "Manage views…", icon: "hero-cog-6-tooth", path: ~p"/views"}]}
  chips={[{"view", "Status: Overdue", :fixed} | @chips]}
  sort={State.sort_value(@state)}
  sorts={[
    {"Newest first", "placed:desc"},
    {"Oldest first", "placed:asc"},
    {"Customer A–Z", "customer:asc"},
    {"Largest total", "total:desc"}
  ]}
>
  <:filter key="status" label="Status">
    <.select id="filter-status" name="status" multiple full_width
      value={State.values(@state.filters["status"])} placeholder="Any status">
      <:option :for={{label, value} <- @statuses} value={value}>{label}</:option>
    </.select>
  </:filter>
  <:filter key="owner" label="Owner">
    <.combobox id="filter-owner" name="owner" multiple full_width
      value={State.values(@state.filters["owner"])} placeholder="Anyone">
      <:option :for={{label, value} <- @owners} value={value}>{label}</:option>
    </.combobox>
  </:filter>
  <:save>
    <.button size="sm" variant="outline" phx-click="save_view">Save view</.button>
  </:save>
</.table_toolbar>
```

```html
<div id="orders-toolbar" class="table-toolbar" data-views>

    <div class="table-toolbar-row">
      <nav id="orders-toolbar-views" data-tab-nav aria-label="Views" class="tab-nav table-toolbar-views">
        <div class="tabs tabs-box tab-nav-list">
          <div class="tab-nav-tabs" data-tab-nav-tabs>
            <a href="#all" data-phx-link="patch" data-phx-link-state="push" class="tab" data-index="0" data-tab-nav-item>
              <span class="tab-nav-label">
                All orders
              </span>
              <span class="tab-count">240</span>
            </a>
            <a href="#open" data-phx-link="patch" data-phx-link-state="push" class="tab" data-index="1" data-tab-nav-item>

                Open

              <span class="tab-count">48</span>

            <a href="#overdue" data-phx-link="patch" data-phx-link-state="push" class="tab tab-active" aria-current="page" data-index="2" data-tab-nav-item>
              <span class="tab-nav-label">
                Overdue<span class="table-toolbar-edited"><span class="sr-only">(edited)</span></span>
              </span>
```

## Without views

HEEx:

```heex
<.table_toolbar
  id="customers-toolbar"
  search={@state.search}
  placeholder="Search customers"
  shown={length(@rows)}
  total={@total}
  noun={{"customer", "customers"}}
  chips={State.chips(@state, ["plan"], %{"plan" => @plans})}
  sort={State.sort_value(@state)}
  sorts={[{"Name A–Z", "name:asc"}, {"Most orders", "orders:desc"}, {"Newest", "joined:desc"}]}
>
  <:filter key="plan" label="Plan">
    <.select id="filter-plan" name="plan" multiple full_width
      value={State.values(@state.filters["plan"])} placeholder="Any plan">
      <:option :for={{label, value} <- @plans} value={value}>{label}</:option>
    </.select>
  </:filter>
  <:more><.button size="sm" variant="outline" phx-click="export">Export</.button></:more>
</.table_toolbar>
```

```html
                <div class="popover-panel absolute z-50 mt-1 hidden w-full p-1" data-select-panel>
                  <div id="customers-toolbar-sort-list" role="listbox" class="max-h-72 overflow-auto" data-select-list>
                    <button type="button" tabindex="-1" role="option" aria-selected="true" class="combo-item" data-select-item data-value="" data-selected>
                      <span class="hero-check size-4 shrink-0" aria-hidden="true"></span>
                      <span data-label class="truncate">Name A–Z</span>
                    </button>
                    <button type="button" tabindex="-1" role="option" aria-selected="false" class="combo-item" data-select-item data-value="orders:desc">
                      <span class="hero-check size-4 shrink-0 opacity-0" aria-hidden="true"></span>
                      <span data-label class="truncate">Most orders</span>
                    </button>
                    <button type="button" tabindex="-1" role="option" aria-selected="false" class="combo-item" data-select-item data-value="joined:desc">
                      <span class="hero-check size-4 shrink-0 opacity-0" aria-hidden="true"></span>
                      <span data-label class="truncate">Newest</span>
                    </button>
                  </div>
                </div>
              </div>
            </label>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="sheet-footer">
        <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost" phx-click="[[&quot;push&quot;,{&quot;value&quot;:{&quot;table&quot;:&quot;customers-toolbar&quot;},&quot;event&quot;:&quot;dt:reset&quot;}]]">
          Clear all
        </button>
        <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary ml-auto grow sm:grow-0" phx-click="[[&quot;dispatch&quot;,{&quot;to&quot;:&quot;#customers-toolbar-filters&quot;,&quot;event&quot;:&quot;shadcn:hide-modal&quot;}]]">
          Show 3 customers
        </button>
      </div>
      <div id="customers-toolbar-filters-toasts" data-toast-host phx-update="ignore"></div>
    </dialog>
  </form>
</div>
```

# Timeline

A vertical or horizontal sequence of events.

## Specs

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Timeline list | <ul class=timeline> of vertically stacked events. |
| Middle marker | Centered icon node (check/clock) on the spine. |
| Box | timeline-box card holding the event label. |
| Connector | <hr> spine segments tinted with border-color. |

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Box radius | var(--radius-md) |
| Box border | 1px border-color |
| Box shadow | var(--shadow-xs) |
| Box font | 0.875rem |
| Spine | <hr> tinted border-color |

Tokens used: `card`, `border-color`, `primary`, `muted-foreground`

## Accessibility

Role / ARIA: Presentational <ul>/<li>; marker icons are aria-hidden decoration.

Focus: Not focusable; no interactive elements.

Screen reader: Event labels read in order as a list; icons are hidden from the accessibility tree.

Touch target: Not interactive; no hit-target requirement.

Reduced motion: Static; no animation to suppress.

## Native (SwiftUI)

Parity: partial - some web features are not yet native.

```swift
List(events) { event in
    Label(event.title, systemImage: event.done ? "checkmark.circle" : "clock")
}
.listStyle(.plain)
```

A plain List with leading status icons approximates the vertical spine.

## Default

```html
<ul class="timeline">
  <li>
    <div class="timeline-middle"><span class="hero-check-circle size-4 text-primary" aria-hidden="true"></span></div>
    <div class="timeline-end timeline-box">Project kickoff</div>
    <hr />
  </li>
  <li>
    <hr />
    <div class="timeline-middle"><span class="hero-check-circle size-4 text-primary" aria-hidden="true"></span></div>
    <div class="timeline-end timeline-box">Design complete</div>
    <hr />
  </li>
  <li>
    <hr />
    <div class="timeline-middle"><span class="hero-clock size-4 text-muted-foreground" aria-hidden="true"></span></div>
    <div class="timeline-end timeline-box">Launch</div>
  </li>
</ul>
```
